main_text.p: caufla fefe receperunt,&in eis miferri- mam uitam egerunt: commiseratione, fi afflictiones: laude autem,fi uirtutem in fi de spe&es, digni sunt. Notum enim eft illud Apoftolicum di&um: Oberrauerut cum ouillis & caprinis pellibus,deftituti, opprefsi,male habiti,quibus indignus e- rat mundus,in defertis errantes,& montibus ac fpeluncis & cauernis terrę: Heb. 11.37.38. Nihil autem dubium eft hofce, fi modo per fæuitiam tyrannorum licuif- fet,ad fua redire paratos fuiffe, ac oppor- tunitate oblata pie ufos effe, ut uel unius Heliae exemplum monet.

Proxime ad illos accefsiffe uidentur, qui praepotentibus æmulis,& armatis au &oritate publica, [illegible, ~16 letters] bi pacis cauffa cedendum iudicauerunt, ne praefentia fua Ecclefijs maiores motus & turbas etiam inuiti parerent: & ut liberius pijs ftudijs, ac fuæ aliorumq; inftitutioni operam dare poffent. In horũ numero fuerunt Hieronymus Stridonen fis, & Gregorius Naziazenus, & alij quidam: qui tamé non deerant fuo muneri, cum & facros libros uiua uoce in coetu piorum auditorum,& eruditis commen

page.notes: The Greek phrase after "publica," (in the printed line "&oritate publica, ...") is too blurred to read letter by letter; it is marked illegible. The Greek is set in Greek type and is not transcribed. "aliorumq;" is read from a printed "q;" abbreviation with a tilde-like sign. The word "de spe&es" is read as printed with the ligature. Catchword "tarijs," is at the foot right. The reference "Heb. 11.37.38." stands in the running text, not as a marginal note; there are no marginal notes on this page.
